# T7.02: H.264 High profile with CABAC

We encoded H.264 Main with CAVLC. nullmoth's `libnvenc_h264`, traced with `ProfileLevel = H264_High_AutoLevel` and
`H264EntropyMode = CABAC` against Main (`docs/traces/h264high/`, `tools/h264setup.c` prints the differing fields), changes
five fields and nothing in the pushed methods:

| field | Main / CAVLC | High / CABAC |
|---|---|---|
| `sps_data.profile_idc` | 77 | 100 |
| `pps_data.entropy_coding_mode_flag` | 0 | 1 |
| `pps_data.transform_8x8_mode_flag` | 0 | 1 |
| `md_control.intra_luma8x8_mode_enable` | 0 | 0x1ff (all nine 8x8 intra modes) |
| `md_control.priority_ipred_type_ip1` | 1 | 3 |

Our SPS/PPS writer already handled profile 100, CABAC and the 8x8 transform. `EncConfig.h264_profile` / `cabac` now
select them. `libnvencvt` defaults to **High + CABAC + 8x8**; `ProfileLevel` Main gives Main + CABAC (CAVLC if
`H264EntropyMode` asks for it), Baseline gives Main + CAVLC as before (a P-only CAVLC stream).

## Results (`vttest`, 20 Mbit/s CBR, Apple's software decoder)

| size | Main + CAVLC | Main + CABAC | High + CABAC + 8x8 | engine time CAVLC -> High |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1920x1080 | 53.75 dB | - | 55.40 dB | 2.47 -> 2.93 ms |
| 3840x2160 | 31.9-32.5 dB | 49.2 dB | 49.3-49.7 dB | 4.71 -> 7.21 ms |

CABAC is what made the difference at 4K (our CAVLC streams were starved at that rate); it costs engine time (CABAC is
serial), 2.5 ms per 4K frame. OBS (`obs-rec.sh`, profile high / baseline): `h264 (High)` with CABAC + 8x8, and Main with
CAVLC; 0 decode errors.
